digest.component_or_area: plan-review gate, model escalation and window sizing
propositions: models_at_or_above() fails to locate non-Anthropic-family primaries in MODEL_LADDER, falls through to returning the entire ladder instead of a single-element list, causing escalation to propose smaller windows and cross provider families.

largest_window_tokens() returns the ladder maximum (1000000) for unlocated primaries instead of a conservative minimum, causing P8 to under-block material that will not fit, leading to truncation instead of decomposition advice.

The prerequisite-coverage escalation path (prerequisites.py:260-263) consumes the full unlocated ladder and selects the first rung (claude-haiku-4-5), crossing provider families for non-Anthropic primaries.

For non-Anthropic primaries, the one-criterion retry (the most likely to succeed) is bypassed when the batch call context-limits, because escalation immediately attempts smaller-window rungs before returning to the operator's own model.
The defect is invisible on the default configuration (claude-opus-4-8) but lands exactly on custom deployments that set REBAR_LLM_MODEL to a non-Anthropic provider model.
